title: Pillbox accelerating cavity: TM010 of a copper cylinder 10 mm in radius and 13.06 mm long (a half-wave cell), on its axis for a particle at the speed of light
source: The pillbox's TM010 mode in closed form, E_z = E0 J0(χ01 r/R) (T. P. Wangler, RF Linear Accelerators, 2nd ed., Wiley 2008, §2.3): f = χ01 c/(2πR); the transit-time factor T = sin(x)/x with x = ωL/(2c); the stored energy U = ½ ε0 E0² π R² L J1²(χ01), so R/Q = (E0 L T)²/(ωU) = 2 L T²/(ω ε0 π R² J1²(χ01)); Q0 = (R/δ)/(1 + R/L) with copper's skin depth δ at f; the shunt impedance (R/Q) Q0. Evaluated apart from the code under test

quantities.reason: 2 mm tetrahedra at order 2 on a faceted cylinder: +9e-5 GHz (+4e-5 at 1.5 mm)
E_z along the axis integrated by three-point Gauss–Legendre on 400 intervals: within 2e-6
the voltage and the stored energy from the same field, its amplitude cancelling: within 2e-3 Ω
the wall loss by perturbation over the faceted surface: −0.6 % at 2 mm, −0.4 % at 1.5 mm
Q0's error, R/Q's being far smaller
